claims.statement: For a rational recognizable series with state dimension r and all reduced realization numerators/denominators at most 2^H, evaluated on a jointly strictly upper-triangular rational tuple of dimension D whose entry heights are at most 2^B, every output entry has denominator dividing Q*=Q_lambda Q_gamma (Q_A Q_X)^(D-1), with log2 Q* <= 2rH+(D-1)(nr^2H+nD^2B). A deterministic per-entry rounded exact oracle with at least 2 log2 Q*+2 fractional bits can be reconstructed exactly by continued fractions, preserving an adaptive exact learner transcript subject to a charged rational-query-generation interface.
assumptions: The target has a rational linear realization of dimension r
Every input tuple is jointly strictly upper triangular
All realization and query rational-entry heights are bounded as supplied parameters
The exact learner's adaptive query generation and bit complexity are explicitly charged
claims.status: INTERNALLY_DERIVED_CYCLE2_CANDIDATE; PRIMARY PRIOR ART NOT CLEARED
claims.novelty_boundary: Rational reconstruction is classical. The local contribution is the explicit denominator bound for this finite nilpotent evaluation and its transcript/precision accounting. It is not a numerical stability theorem for arbitrary characteristic-zero series and does not validate L01.

costs.returned_bits: T D^2 times fractional precision plus charged integer-range bits
costs.reconstruction_time: T D^2 poly(log Q*, H, B, log(nrD)) bit operations, plus learner arithmetic
costs.input_bits: All rational query-entry descriptions charged; adaptive size growth is not bounded for a general learner

claims.falsifier: A rational response entry outside the stated denominator bound or a distinct rational with denominator <=Q* within the reconstruction radius would refute the claim.
claims.next_gate: Independent algebra review and a finite exact-versus-rounded adaptive transcript implementation.

claims.statement: For f_w(u)=1[u=w], w in [n]^d, minimal Hankel rank is d+1. One exact full-matrix rational query of dimension d+1 identifies w under sum_i X_i^T X_i <= I with polynomial input/output bit costs. Under the reconstructed adaptive full-matrix Gaussian oracle with fixed variance sigma^2 and the same per-query excitation cap, any zero-vs-hidden-word test with both errors <=delta has expected total query dimension and returned scalar entries at least 2 sigma^2 n^d kl(1-delta,delta).
assumptions: n>=2 and d>=1
The exact input and output are rational and exact
For the noisy interface every returned matrix entry receives independent Gaussian noise of variance sigma^2
Each query obeys the aggregate per-call excitation constraint
C is expected total query dimension under the zero target
The test must distinguish zero from every hidden word with both errors <= delta < 1/2
claims.novelty_boundary: A finite exact-versus-noisy interface counterexample only. It does not refute or verify the universal L01 learner; prior art includes weighted-automaton learning and adaptive Gaussian sensing. Long Astra proof files were unavailable at the pinned commit.

costs.decoder: Polynomial bit time using a known prime-position table

claims.falsifier: An admissible adaptive Gaussian strategy below the bound or a collision in the exact prime-position encoding.
claims.next_gate: Retrieve and independently verify full N25 proof and targeted primary-source search for adaptive noisy noncommutative series evaluation under aggregate excitation.

claims.statement: If a randomized polynomial-time teacher-free learner receives only ordinary trajectories from every binary O(d)-state HMM and returns an efficiently evaluable law Q within constant total variation of the source, then the learner yields a search-LPN predictor, and Goldreich-Levin plus fresh correlations recovers the hidden parity under the standard search-LPN hardness assumption.
assumptions: Noisy-parity hardness at a fixed noise rate eta<1/2
The output law or next-bit conditional evaluator is polynomial-time evaluable at required precision
Training access is ordinary passive trajectories only
The process may include the clocked parity automaton construction
claims.novelty_boundary: Kearns et al. already give the PFA noisy-parity evaluator hardness mechanism; the HMM paper records the standard consequence. The local TV threshold and cost ledger are not a new hardness result.

costs.training: Each reset trajectory simulates one LPN example; charge all observed tokens and learner memory/runtime
costs.extractor: Polynomial evaluator calls and Goldreich-Levin time
costs.precision: Polynomial bits for joint probabilities at scale 2^-d theta

claims.falsifier: A polynomial-time passive learner satisfying the stated evaluator/TV interface together with a search-LPN solver separation would falsify the conditional implication's hardness consequence.
claims.next_gate: Attack the stronger teacher-assisted fresh-prefix recurrence question separately; do not transfer this passive lower bound to chosen-prefix oracles.

claims.statement: In the stationary two-state deterministic-emission HMM with A->B probability epsilon and B->B probability theta in {1/4,3/4}, every learner using at most B passive symbols has worst-case expected absolute error in P(Y_{t+1}=1|Y_t=1) at least (1-4B epsilon)/4 when epsilon<=1/8; adaptively selecting a feature after observing the transcript cannot overcome the identical all-zero event.
assumptions: Stationary initialization
At most B total observed symbols across streams/resets
The target is worst-history conditional prediction after the rare symbol
epsilon<=1/8
claims.novelty_boundary: A scoped rare-context obstruction consistent with established spectral learning singular-value dependencies. It is not a lower bound for stationary-average prediction or fixed-horizon TV approximation.

costs.active_resets: Would change the interface and must be charged

claims.falsifier: An estimator whose transcript-conditioned output differs on the identical all-zero record under the two target HMMs would refute the coupling proof.
claims.next_gate: Test only with a costed active reset/conditional sampler or a supplied lower bound on context mass/Hankel singular value.

claims.statement: A clocked O(T)-state source that emits uniform X_i and M_i=1{X_1:i=s_1:i} for an unknown binary word s allows exact recovery of s in T chosen-prefix conditional-sampling queries; the queried prefix probability at step k is 2^{-(k-1)}, while passive identification of the final bit requires Omega(2^T) independent full trajectories for constant error.
assumptions: The family promises the marker mechanism M_i=1 iff the first i random bits match a single fixed hidden word
The oracle can sample a future suffix conditioned on any explicitly chosen prefix, including exponentially rare prefixes
Each conditional sample is a fresh independent draw
claims.novelty_boundary: An explicit oracle-versus-passive sample-cost witness on a supplied clocked family, not a new general learner. Liu-Moitra's arbitrary-low-rank chosen-prefix result appears to subsume the positive direction.

costs.passive_samples: Omega(2^T) for final-bit identification; naive rejection simulation costs about 2^T episodes

claims.falsifier: A passive test with o(2^T) full trajectories and constant worst-case success on the pair differing only in s_T, or a conditional sample that does not reveal the next hidden bit under a matched prefix.
claims.next_gate: Compare physical/experimental conditional-query cost with passive sampling and verify the automaton convention/source prior-art details.

claims.statement: For hidden Z=s·A and R independent noisy readouts of that same persistent Z per episode, N=d+ceil(log2(2/delta)) passive random input episodes and odd R>=2 beta^-2 log(2N/delta) recover s with probability >=1-delta; the recovered mask gives a two-coordinate online predictive recurrence with unit-norm states and readout norm <=sqrt(2) for every bounded future task.
assumptions: A is uniform GF(2)^d per reset
Readout errors are independent conditional on the same latent parity
Known rational eta with 1-2eta>=beta>0
claims.status: INTERNALLY_PROVED_NARROW_SUBCLASS; MATCHED DIRECT DECODER HAS IDENTICAL COST; NO PRIORITY CLAIM

costs.memory: O(d^2+R) working bits plus d model bits
costs.readouts: Per task/cut, 2M simulated futures with M>=ceil((2rho^2)^-1 log(8/delta)); finite-bit rational sampling cost detailed in child report

claims.falsifier: A failure of the majority/rank proof under the specified iid reset design, or a future law not determined by current parity and phase.
claims.novelty_boundary: Independent repeated readouts are load-bearing; same-data majority/GF(2) decoder has identical acquisition cost. No arbitrary-HMM advantage is claimed.

claims.statement: For rho=2^-n, P_b emits n fair bits X and terminal Y=b only on X=0^n, otherwise Y fair; the common exact teacher Q is uniform. Both worlds satisfy KL(P_b||Q)=rho ln 2. Any algorithm using m<=2^(n-2) passive P-trajectories and unlimited Q calls fails to return a 1/3-TV accurate terminal predictor at the rare prefix with success 2/3 in both worlds. This lower bound applies only to uniform all-prefix prediction; Q itself has actual-path squared conditional-TV loss <=zeta/(4 ln 2), so A06's average-path target is not refuted.
assumptions: Finite horizon n+1; complete passive P trajectories
Same positive exact-rational teacher Q in both worlds
The tested target demands a conditional guarantee at every explicitly supplied prefix
claims.novelty_boundary: Direct two-world Le Cam calculation for a strengthened uniform-prefix target. The average-path boundary follows the source A06 Hellinger lemma. No canonical recurrence impossibility is established.

costs.passive: More than 2^(n-2) trajectories necessary for stated uniform prediction success; n+1 symbols per trajectory
costs.teacher: Unlimited exact Q queries have zero distinguishing value because Q is identical in both worlds
costs.source_conditional_control: One P-conditional suffix sample at prefix 0^n recovers b; prefix description costs n bits

claims.falsifier: A predictor satisfying the uniform target on both worlds with <=2^(n-2) P samples would contradict the exact transcript-TV calculation.
claims.next_gate: Attack A06 actual-path stable fresh-prefix recurrence directly; do not claim this lower bound settles it.

claims.statement: For the supplied uniform parity-clock family P_s versus Q_L with unknown nonzero s in GF(2)^L, any fixed bank of M bounded path tests has a worst mask with moment-vector gap at most sqrt(M/[4(2^L-1)]) even though path TV is 1/2. An adaptive exact population-expectation service identifies s in L+1 scalar queries using O(L^2) total query-description and answer bits; the first signal gap is 2^-L, so sample-mean simulation takes O(4^L log(L/delta)) paths. If noiseless individual reset paths are retained, ordinary homogeneous equations recover s with L+O(log(1/delta)) paths by GF(2) elimination.
assumptions: The source is promised to be Q_L or one of P_s, where the unknown nonzero mask is a homogeneous parity over the first L observed bits
Adaptive scalar service returns exact population expectations, or answers to the stated precision
Raw-path positive result requires independent reset trajectories and exact noiseless bits
claims.status: INTERNALLY_DERIVED_PARITY_CLASS_WITNESS; CLASSICAL PARITY LEARNING; NO NOVELTY OR GENERAL ADAPTIVITY ADVANTAGE
claims.novelty_boundary: The expectation oracle is stronger than path samples and has an exponentially small first signal. The raw-data GF(2) learner is standard noiseless parity learning. The result is a supplied parity-family counterexample to blanket fixed-dictionary or adaptive impossibility claims, not general HMM acquisition.

costs.exact_population_oracle: L+1 queries; O(L^2) query and answer bits; O(L) memory and O(L^2) caller-side bit operations; service-side computation unspecified
costs.sample_mean_simulation: O(4^L log(L/delta)) reset paths under the stated uniform Hoeffding allocation; L times as many observed symbols
costs.raw_paths: L+O(log(1/delta)) independent resets; O(L^2+L log(1/delta)) observed bits and GF(2) elimination; O(L^2) memory

claims.falsifier: Any fixed bank violating the Parseval separation bound or any adaptive exact query protocol answer trace inconsistent with its stated Fourier coefficient calculation.
claims.next_gate: A useful advancement must handle an unsupplied hidden structure or a weaker realistic query service and beat the same-data raw-example baseline.
